content: The law of identity in logic asserts that an object is identical to itself, symbolically represented as A ≡ A. This principle is upheld in any reflexive relation, and when discussing equality, the statement A is A is considered a tautology, meaning it is self-evidently true. In philosophy, this law is often incorrectly attributed to Aristotle. However, Aristotle did not explicitly formulate it in this way. Instead, Wilhelm Wundt credited Gottfried Leibniz with the symbolic expression A is A. In 2002, Jonathon Keats organized a petition in Berkeley, California, to establish A = A as statutory law. The proposed legislation stated that every entity shall be identical to itself. The law also included a provision that any entity found to be non-identical to itself would face a fine of up to one-tenth of a cent. Despite its creative premise, the law was not passed. However, it inspired a similar petition effort in Santa Cruz, California.
